data.title: Destroyed crops, riverbed cyclists and a ‘Rock of Starvation’: how drought has devastated the Danube
data.description: The Guardian travelled 100 miles along the EU’s longest river, where some residents are struggling to secure drinking water For centuries, the rock was seen as a warning. When it began to emerge from the Danube, beneath Gellért Hill in Budapest, it meant the river had fallen so low that floating mills could no longer operate, crops were probably failing, and hunger would almost certainly follow. That is why, in the Hungarian capital, where over time the boulder became little more than a legend, it was named Ínség-szikla – the Rock of Starvation. Today, amid record-low water levels on the Danube, the rock has not only emerged from the water, but surfaced almost in its entirety, along with the sandy riverbed on which it rests, astonishing geologists and government scientists sent to examine it. And, much as the rock was said to warn, Hungary is now facing an unprecedented energy crisis that has forced the country to shut down all but one of its Danube-cooled nuclear reactors for the first time in 44 years. data.title: The moment I knew: I heard her beautiful laugh again, and all my emotions came flooding back
data.description: Eddie Botha felt an easy connection with Jennifer. But when she went away for a trip, he thought that was the end of their growing romance Find more stories from the moment I knew series I met Jennifer at a Guy Sebastian concert in Kuala Lumpur in 2005. It was strange I was there because I’m kind of anti-pop music, but we were introduced there by a mutual friend. We didn’t talk that much but I immediately liked Jen and invited her to dinner the following week. That first date wasn’t in a fancy restaurant and we sat in the corner and talked for over an hour. I liked that she wasn’t at all bothered by the simplicity of the dining room. Being a foreigner in Malaysia, I immediately felt with Jen that there wasn’t as much of a culture gap as I’d felt with others. I could talk to her easily and was struck by her warmth and openness. And it was there that I first heard her laugh beaming out across the room, a pure, joyous sound. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I don’t even drink whisky’: Scotland reels in visitors as much of Europe swelters
data.description: More direct flights from North America and, say tourism chiefs, Highland warriors and Tartan Army have helped For the tourist industry, 2026 has been a rocky year, with war, EU border delays, climate and economic woes gnawing away at holiday plans. But while much of Britain is feeling the loss of visitors from the Middle East and beyond, one part is thriving. Scotland is reeling in ever more visitors, with strong annual growth and a 15% rise in flight bookings to Scottish airports in June and July, compared with a drop in bookings to London and the rest of England in recent months, according to VisitBritain figures. data.title: Christopher Berry-Dee is the UK’s all-time bestselling true crime author. Is he also a violent abuser of women and children?
data.description: The British writer is known for his unique ability to get inside the heads of serial killers. But a Guardian investigation reveals multiple accusations of assault and child sexual abuse. What is the truth about the man described by his own daughter as ‘absolute evil’? Warning: this article contains descriptions of sexual abuse and violence From the outside, it looked like the sort of happy family home a child might draw. Red brick, surrounded by rolling countryside, in Curdridge, near Winchester. Here lived the true crime writer Christopher Berry-Dee, with his second wife, Tracey Dee, and their two young daughters, Zoe and Sasha, in the early 1990s. Inside, it was a house of horrors, full of murder memorabilia. In a wardrobe were the clothes a nine-year-old girl had been murdered in. One afternoon, Zoe was playing when she found them. The now 38-year-old council worker from Romsey says she remembers “putting it all on … going downstairs and everyone being absolutely traumatised”. Later, another gruesome memento was added to the collection: the Austin Metro that convicted murderer Michael Sams had used to transport a body in 1991. Bloodied sections of the seatbelts had been cut out for forensic tests. Berry-Dee was the serial killer man. He wrote to convicted murderers in jail and befriended them. They told him everything. Through them he saw the terror in their victims’ eyes, watched their anguished death throes, heard their final screams. He listened to tapes of their confessions in his study. Zoe grew used to hearing them echo through the house. “It would always be on,” she says. “At the time, it felt normal.” Continue reading...

data.title: Are you tweaking on your partner? From secret boob jobs to Botox on the sly, people explain why they keep their cosmetic procedures hidden
data.description: Daniel’s boyfriend thinks his youthful complexion is down to fancy skincare, and Jessica’s nearest and dearest still don’t know she’s had a breast enhancement … Jessica was at a spa with her friends of more than 20 years when she noticed one stare at her bikini, lock eyes with her and laugh, before asking: “Wait, have you …?” The game was up – eight months after she’d had a secret breast enhancement, she’d been rumbled. Fearing judgment from even her closest circle, she had only spoken to two people who’d had the procedure, for advice, and told a neighbour in case she was unwell after the surgery. “My family still don’t know – most people don’t,” the 42-year-old from London says, including her two children who live between her and her ex-husband. “I’m not alone; I’ve since learned winter is the most popular time for people to get things done, then they can just hide under jumpers while everything settles in, so no one notices.” For years, celebrities have endured public speculation about their tweakments and surgeries – but as procedures become more commonplace, “civilian” patients are facing the same questions from family and friends. And many of them are choosing to go incognito; some surgeons estimate up to 70% of their clients aren’t telling others about their aesthetic procedures. But what are the practicalities of disguising everything from breast augmentation to filler to hair transplants from your closest circle? And why are so many people spending thousands of pounds to alter their appearance – only to hope that no one notices? Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv faces missile barrage after Zelenskyy targets Russian satellite network
data.description: Kyiv mayor says attack has caused fires in at least two districts; Ukraine hits Russian rocket facility in long-range strike. What we know on day 1,636 Russian forces launched a missile ⁠attack on Kyiv early on Sunday, sparking fires in ⁠at least ⁠two districts of the Ukrainian capital, the city’s mayor said. Kyiv’s ⁠military administration said one person had been injured. Witnesses reported explosions in the city amid air alerts that sounded after 2am. Mayor Vitali Klitschko, writing on ⁠Telegram, said falling ​debris had ‌caused a ‌fire in a non-residential part of ‌a northern suburb. Several cars were on fire, and another fire had broken out in an area just south of the city ‌centre, he said. Unofficial ​Telegram channels posted photos of what were described as market stalls ablaze. Russia ‌has in ​recent ​weeks been staging intensive air attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine says long-range strikes hit a Russian military airfield and a rocket centre ⁠that supports ⁠Russia’s nascent Starlink-style satellite ​internet network . President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday said Flamingo cruise missiles struck the rocket facility, about 900km from Ukraine’s border, as part of Kyiv’s campaign to pressure Moscow to end ⁠the war by targeting sites deep inside Russia. “It is important that Russia’s war potential be reduced. Peace is needed, and this must be evident in Russia – through concrete damage ⁠to specific facilities,” Zelenskyy wrote on X. He said the airfield hosted aircraft used to attack Ukraine. Ukraine’s armed forces said direct hits were ‌recorded at the airfield in Russia’s ‌Nizhny Novgorod region and the Progress rocket centre in Samara region, sparking fires ‌at both sites. The Samara plant produces rockets used to launch satellites for the Rassvet broadband network, which Russia is developing as an alternative to SpaceX’s Starlink . Starlink operates in Ukraine but not in Russia, giving Kyiv an advantage in drone operations and battlefield communications. In Samara region, local officials said air defences had repelled a “massive missile attack”. “Samara’s industrial infrastructure ‌sustained localised damage,” Ivan Noskov, head of the regional capital, said in an online post. Emergency services were working at the scene, he said. Russia has ⁠asked Washington and ⁠Ankara ⁠to explain reports ​of possible plans ⁠to transfer to Kyiv a “substantial ⁠arsenal” ​of ‌US weapons ‌and ammunition ‌held by Turkey , a spokesperson for Russia’s foreign ministry said ‌on Saturday. Such a transfer would ​cause “serious harm … to our bilateral relations ⁠with Washington and ​Ankara,” the spokesperson ​said in ​a ‌statement. A Russian strike on an apartment block in south-eastern Ukraine on Saturday killed a three-month-old baby and wounded 11 people, local officials said. Drones hit the building in the town of Marhanets, said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration. Russia’s defence ​ministry on Saturday said in the ‌past 24 hours its drones ​and missiles had ​struck Ukrainian logistics centres and energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army, as well as assembly workshops for long-range drones and drone boats. North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has told Russian president Vladimir Putin in a letter that he was “proud” of their countries’ strong ties , state media reported. North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow’s war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say. Kim added that he had a “firm belief” that Russia would thrive and defend its “territorial integrity” under Putin’s “wise leadership”. In a letter to Kim delivered on Friday to mark Korea’s liberation from Japanese colonial rule at the end of the second world war, Putin said relations between the two countries had reached the “unprecedentedly high level of comprehensive strategic partnership” . “Our states are actively cooperating in all the sectors while making concerted efforts to ensure the regional security and stability,” the Russian leader said. The exchange of letters follows Ukraine’s accusation this month that Moscow had launched North Korean ballistic missiles in a strike that killed at least nine people and wounded dozens. Kyiv has also recently said that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are due to deploy to Russia, although it has provided no evidence to back the claim or a timeframe for the deployment. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump shows off article on lower drug prices that says Biden deserves credit, not him
data.description: US president credits himself with lowest drug prices in 60 years, when article says drop is more likely due to Biden The White House flooded social media on Saturday with an image of Donald Trump showing off the recent Washington Post headline “Prescription drug prices record sharpest drop in more than 60 years”, but failed to mention that experts cited in the article actually attributed the price drop to Joe Biden, not Trump. On its official accounts, the White House triumphantly captioned the photograph of Trump: “POV: you bring the receipts.” Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, also shared it. Continue reading...

data.title: Rescue teams search for survivors in Indonesia after powerful earthquake
data.description: Searchers dig through collapsed buildings and debris after 7.7 magnitude quake killed at least 47 people Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia on Sunday as they searched for bodies and possible survivors a day after a powerful earthquake killed at least 47 people, injured more than 100 and displaced thousands. At least 24 people died in Manggarai regency and 17 in neighbouring East Manggarai, with additional fatalities reported in Sikka, Ngada and Ende regencies, the national disaster management agency said. Rescuers were still searching for people feared buried beneath landslides triggered by the quake across six regencies on Flores, a predominantly Catholic island in Muslim-majority Indonesia. Continue reading...

data.title: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
data.description: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. data.translatedDescription: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. data.title: Community Shield offers insight into Arsenal’s desire and Maresca’s Manchester City impact | Jonathan Wilson
data.description: Wembley curtain-raiser can offer clues but it is no reliable pointer to a season – its winners have not landed the title since 2018 The doubt for anyone when a long-strived-for goal has been achieved is hunger. Arsenal waited 22 years for their 14th league title and, compounding the yearning, finished second three times in a row before finally lifting the Premier League trophy in May. The physical exertions of last season were immense – as seen by Declan Rice’s clear exhaustion and Bukayo Saka’s intermittent contributions at the World Cup, where William Saliba picked up a back injury – but so too was the emotional strain. The first weeks of a new season after a major tournament, especially the World Cup, are often a little erratic anyway, but this feels like a particularly unpredictable start to a campaign. Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs have changed manager this summer. For the first time in 40 years, none of the five big managerial beasts of the Premier League era – Sir Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola – will be in charge of a club. There are unknowns and uncertainty everywhere, even at Arsenal. Mikel Arteta may be the longest-serving manager in the league but there are questions even there; it would be no great surprise if Arsenal were to start slowly. Continue reading...

data.title: Novak Djokovic suffers in Cincinnati heat as Thiago Agustín Tirante inflicts shock defeat
data.description: Argentinian powers to 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 victory Heat and humidity take toll on Djokovic Fery holds off Duckworth  6-4, 2-6 7-6(4) The scoreboard did not yet indicate that anything was awry, but even as Novak Djokovic led by a set in his opening match at the Cincinnati Open, he was already struggling badly. From the second set onwards, he spent much of his time between points squatting and bending over as he desperately tried to catch his breath in the notorious Ohioan humidity. He was eventually dispatched 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 by Thiago Agustín Tirante of Argentina, who took this golden opportunity to register the biggest win of his career. Continue reading...

data.title: La Liga 2026-27 preview: Madrid look to Mourinho in bid to dethrone Barcelona
data.description: Florentino Pérez pressed the Special One button again after two straight trophyless seasons at Real, but Lamine Yamal and co remain title favourites A lot has changed since José Mourinho was last appointed Real Madrid manager, but a lot has also not changed. Before his first game in charge in 2010, Spain had just become world champions , their extra-time winner in the final scored by a Barcelona player after their opponents, who had been reduced to 10 men, had tried to kick them off the park. Like then, Mourinho’s task is to take down a Barcelona team that have won two La Liga titles in succession . And like then, he has a host of world-class talent at his disposal. Florentino Pérez is also still around – and he is largely the reason why Mourinho is back. After the chief executive, José Ángel Sánchez, was said to have led the charge to appoint Xabi Alonso last summer, the 79-year-old club president has made the decision his own this time. He promised Mourinho, who won La Liga with 100 points in his first spell, would return if he was re-elected in snap elections in June and the announcement came , in true Pérez style, on the opening day of the World Cup. Continue reading...

data.title: Women’s U20 World Cup boycott may hurt in short term but can send Fifa a vital message | Tom Garry
data.description: Women’s football has much to gain from the kind of reforms that threats to snub upcoming tournaments might prompt. Infantino should be taken on “And I say to all the women … Pick the right battles. Pick the right fights. You have the power to change. You have the power to convince us men what we have to do and what we don’t have to do. You do it. Just do it. With men, with Fifa, you will find open doors. Just push the doors. They are open.” Those were the condescending words of Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino , three years ago during a tone-deaf speech in Sydney, which left his audience, including some of the most senior women in the game, exasperated. It is a damning indictment of Infantino’s tenure that his patronising monologue on the eve of the Women’s World Cup final now barely even creeps into the top 10 of the most controversial moments since his latest re-election, in March 2023. Continue reading...

data.title: London City Lionesses’ Mapi León: ‘It is a club created for women. It is beautiful and exciting’
data.description: Spain defender on swapping Barcelona for Bromley, embracing the contrasting style of the WSL – and her newfound love for beans and crumpets ‘No, I can’t, I’m sorry, it’s a secret!” Mapi León roars with laughter, in response to being asked what persuaded her to join London City Lionesses. Does this bode badly for our interview? Fear not, the Spain centre-back is in as banterous and jovial a mood as you could imagine any new signing to be, as she embarks on her first major interview since signing for the Women’s Super League club. Across the course of our conversation, in bright sunshine outside a quiet hotel near Maidstone, it is evident that the 31-year-old could scarcely be happier about her decision to swap Barcelona for south-east England. She is sorely missing her cat, Bagheera (“Here, you ask for so many things for pets, you can’t [really] fly with them, it’s so many documents, so many things”) but, that aside, she is buoyant, relaxed and clearly embracing English life. She says she likes the “little bread” in the morning, and we eventually establish she is referring to crumpets, and reveals: “I like the beans in the morning. It’s really interesting. My Spanish teammates like Alexia [Putellas] and Jana [Fernández] are like: ‘What are you doing eating beans in the morning? You need to train.’ I go: ‘No, it’s fine I like it.’” Continue reading...

data.title: I feel guilt talking to those left behind in Afghanistan. While I enjoy freedom, they are prisoners | Nelufar Hedayat
data.description: Five years since the Taliban returned to power, life – especially for women – is awful. We must keep the people’s stories alive and hope they will be free again There are fewer and fewer stories coming out of the land of my birth. Before, I would open Instagram and see my cousins, lip-syncing to trending videos, posing with flowers at a rose garden or at a trendy cafe in their coolest outfits, keeping a record of their lives. I would hear British-Afghan friends talk about their recent trips to the provinces, towns and cities of their foremothers and the buzz of learning about their heritage. I would eagerly await the latest music video from Afghanistan’s many pop stars, all vying to become the hottest track played at weddings, not just in Afghanistan but all over the world. Afghanistan, its culture, and people felt closer back then. Five years ago today , the brittle peace of the fragile new democracy was shattered by the withdrawal of western military, diplomatic and charitable groups that had intervened in the country’s fate since 2001. Overnight, on Sunday, 15 August 2021, Afghanistan was undone and abandoned. Nelufar Hedayat is an Afghan-British journalist, and the presenter and co-director of the documentary In Real Life: the God Thieves Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: Sure, ‘Woke 1’ had its issues – but we have far bigger problems on our hands | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: AOC’s remarks about past excesses have been ripped out of context. Progressives shouldn’t get roped into this sideshow There is probably no word that has been more used and abused in the last decade than “woke”. It has been rendered completely meaningless, but it refuses to die. Indeed, it has now taken on new life: in the past week, there’s been a flurry of headlines about “Woke 1.0” or “Woke One”. If you haven’t seen the phrase pop up in your newsfeed yet, it will soon. So what is this cursed phrase? There’s no official definition, but the term is largely being used to refer to the period between 2018 and 2021 when social justice language was at its peak in mainstream culture. Certain progressives, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, have started to use “Woke 1” disparagingly, as a way to distance themselves from that period and signal that they stand for a new form of left-leaning politics that is more palatable to centrist Democrats. “Woke 2”, I suppose. Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Alarmed by the alarm: people react to ‘severe alert’ on phones over UK wildfires
data.description: Many complained online that piercingly loud tone was ‘overreach’ while others lamented lack of action on decarbonisation On Friday at 7pm, Thérèse Coffey was nine miles away from a nuclear power station when her phone made a loud, piercing and very worrying sound: it was a “severe” emergency alert . “Was expecting [a] much more specific alert, not a generic message on wildfires,” the former Conservative cabinet minister said on X. She wasn’t alone in being alarmed by the alarm sent to phones in England and Wales. In the aftermath, thousands of social media users expressed their shock at alert. Some shared funny memes and others lamented what they viewed as lack of government action on decarbonisation. Academic John Ritzema called it a “massive overreach” and said the alert system should be “be for ‘drop everything and prepare for something terrible’ situations”, something Coffey echoed, saying alerts should not become commonplace to avoid “Peter cries wolf situations”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Their Strength Through Joy conversation is killing me’: Samuel Beckett’s German diaries
data.description: Published for the first time this month, the Irish writer’s record of his months in pre-war Germany is a fascinating insight into his understanding of, and unease with, Nazism War was not yet on the immediate horizon when Samuel Beckett visited the German city of Hamburg in October 1936, but after watching the apoplexy that Adolf Hitler’s braying induced in ordinary Germans, the Irish playwright was certain that peace could not last. “They’ll need to fight soon (or burst),” he noted in his diary on 6 October. The six notebooks that Beckett compiled during his six-month journey across Germany between late September 1936 and April 1937, published for the first time by German publisher Suhrkamp on 20 August this year, put paid to a commonly held view of the author of Waiting for Godot as a poet of pure pessimism, interested in despair and stasis but unconcerned by real-life politics. Continue reading...

data.title: Snapshot review – fun found-footage scarer follows amateur Ripper hunters in the 1880s
data.description: Edinburgh film festival A women’s spiritualist investigation team go after the serial killer, braving evil forces conjured into being by fear, misogyny and political rage Here is a cheerfully ingenious lo-fi movie experiment from first-time feature director Joseph Archer and writer-performer Cathy Wippel; it’s a found-footage horror with hints of Blair Witch and Peeping Tom, set in the Victorian London of Jack the Ripper. The footage that’s been found, incidentally, is composed of unearthed reels of monochrome film from the 1880s, which we see entirely in a kinetoscope-style circular screen, flickering and glitching and buzzing with eerie accidental jump cuts from one weird scene to the next. It was supposedly shot by an enterprising pioneer called Tamworth (we hear his voice from behind the camera, but never see his face), who, it becomes clear, is a sensational and until now unacknowledged genius of early cinema – in that he manages to record lip-sync sound on to wax cylinders so we can actually hear what everyone is saying. With a cheeky touch of implied black comedy, the film is suggesting that Tamworth was somehow able to carry his camera and recording equipment to these places of Victorian horror and underclass shame as easily as an iPhone. Continue reading...

data.title: Little Bird: this beautiful, moving Canadian drama will fill you with visceral anger
data.description: There is dignity and tenderness to this drama based on the real story of the Sixties Scoop – the scandal of First Nations children who were forcibly taken from their parents and adopted by white families Here’s one you’ll like: a man comes home to find his wife handcuffed to the wall and his young children missing. They have been taken by child protection services due to the lack of a fridge in the house, which is treated as a sign of neglect. When he confronts law enforcement officials outside, they beat him to death. Decades later, one of the children, now adopted into a Jewish home in Montreal, goes looking for the family she lost, risking the collapse of her new life to do so. I never said it was a joke. Although it turns out there was a fridge, behind the house. Watching Little Bird (18 August, 9pm, Sky Atlantic), I was reminded that TV is capable of more than mere entertainment, something we lose sight of when we think of it as a purely profit-or loss-making enterprise. I felt the visceral anger and sadness of this story of a First Nations woman caught between cultures, robbed by forces beyond her control and stonewalled by the authorities. Set in Canada, the attitude, if not the events, feel shamefully familiar. Continue reading...

data.title: Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt convinced me to give up on my fashion industry dreams
data.description: I was struggling to make ends meet as an unpaid intern when a sarcastic song from the hit comedy gave me the clarity to walk out It was 3am in the summer of 2017, and I was lying in a triple bunk bed in a hostel in London, listening to the sounds of the 14 other people in my dormitory snoring. I had been working unpaid internships in the fashion industry in London for the past 18 months and living in £12-a-night hostels. When I couldn’t sleep, I would watch TV on my beaten-up phone to drown out the snores. I was watching Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt , an absurdist comedy about a woman who moves to New York after 15 years imprisoned in a doomsday cult’s underground bunker. Her relentless positivity often inspired me to keep going, but on that particular night, the opposite happened: Kimmy gave me the courage to give up. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘From this perspective, the bullfrog feels powerful and mythical’: Steven Scott Grogin’s best phone picture
data.description: The photographer was on an early-morning hike by a lake in Michigan when he spotted the unusually large amphibian, so he dipped his lens below the waterline to get the shot Steven Scott Grogin describes his mornings in Michigan as a ritual. He wakes up at 6am on the dot to get ready for a hike. His favourite lake, once a quarry pit, is a 30-minute walk away, so he tends to arrive by around 7am. “It’s serene and private, and I feel very peaceful there,” Grogin says. “The terrain changes from flat areas to very hilly sections, and there is a lot of biodiversity.” As he circled the lake’s perimeter, he saw this American bullfrog in the water. “It was the largest one I’ve ever seen, around six to eight inches long and very hefty,” he says. “Bullfrogs are predators, but they’re also very skittish, so getting close is difficult.” Continue reading...

data.title: Dawn O’Porter: ‘My greatest fear? Clothes moths – and the imminent threat of world war three‘
data.description: The author and presenter on her heroic auntie, being addicted to chips, and the scary gift she’ll leave her kids Born in Scotland, Dawn O’Porter, 47, studied at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts. She began her career in TV production and during the 00s presented documentaries including Super Slim Me and My Breasts Could Kill Me. In 2014, her debut YA novel, Paper Aeroplanes, was shortlisted for the Waterstones children’s book prize. Her first novel for adults, The Cows, was published in 2017 and became a bestseller. Her new book is Hungry Eyes: A Memoir of Appetite, Ambition and the Odd Bag of Wotsits for Dinner. She lives in London with her husband, the actor Chris O’Dowd, and their two children. When were you happiest? The early days of motherhood. We lived in a sweet little bungalow in LA that had a pool. We threw lots of parties. We had a cute dog and a mad Siamese. Trump had never been president, we’d never heard of coronavirus, Claire’s Accessories was still going strong. Good times. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I longed to play the Bach violin double with my daughter – but then I got MS’
data.description: When multiple sclerosis began to affect her fine motor skills, Shakira Hussein found a way to redesign her dream, rather than give it up altogether At first, I failed to recognise the significance of the deterioration in my violin technique. I was preoccupied by other concerns – the crushing exhaustion that I would describe to my doctors as “not normal tiredness”, the unexplained falls from my bike. I did not draw any connection between these issues and my out-of-tune violin playing. Only when the right side of my body detached itself from my central nervous system to the point where I could no longer pick up a pen or walk without a stick to support myself did the words this feels neurological cross my mind. data.title: Is the US ready for President Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez?
data.description: The New York congresswoman’s power is in the spotlight as people wonder if the stars are finally aligning for her to run for US president in 2028 “They assume that my ambition is positional. They assume that my ambition is a title or a seat. And my ambition is way bigger than that. My ambition is to change this country.” The words were delivered slowly, deliberately and with some steeliness by Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez . Her audience, crammed into the pews of Rockefeller Memorial chapel at the University of Chicago , burst into spontaneous applause. That was in May. In the three months since, the speculation around Ocasio-Cortez’s ambitions – for herself and for America – has only grown louder. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Once I started zooming in, I never stopped’: the mesmerising art of macro photography
data.description: Converts describe a demanding form of capturing nature very close up that has grown in popularity in last few years Vote here for your favourite invertebrate of the year “I always just pray ‘please don’t fly away’,” says Dara Ojo. As a wildlife photographer, he can handle spending minutes, hours and sometimes days waiting for the shot, but insects are not always very cooperative. Ojo is one of an increasing number of photographers turning their lenses towards something smaller: macro photography. This refers to photographing the natural world at an extremely close range, close enough to see the facets of a fly’s eye, or the geometry of a spider’s face. Continue reading...

data.title: Double jeopardy could spell end of state case after Luigi Mangione’s guilty plea
data.description: Defense argues New York cannot try Mangione over same act or offense as federal case in killing of Brian Thompson Luigi Mangione ’s plea to federal stalking charges in UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson’s death has spurred questions about the fate of the separate Manhattan murder case against him, with experts saying New York’s double-jeopardy law could derail that trial. Mangione pleaded guilty to one count of interstate stalking resulting in death, and one count of cyberstalking through use of interstate facilities resulting in death, in connection with the 4 December 2024 shooting outside a Midtown hotel. Both charges carry a potential maximum life sentence. Continue reading...

data.description: The Farallon Islands are grappling with an overwhelming invasion of house mice, significantly disturbing the delicate ecological system. A new eradication initiative involves dropping rodenticide bait from helicopters, driving efforts to restore the natural balance of this unique ecosystem.

data.title: In 1958, the US moved 25 caribou to an Alaska island as emergency food for military personnel
data.description: Following the closure of the military base, a herd of caribou was introduced to enhance food reserves, leading to a dramatic surge in their numbers. With no natural predators or hunting, their population exploded, causing significant overgrazing that harmed the island's delicate flora and soil. This unchecked growth prompted the caribou to migrate to Kagalaska Island, raising new ecological concerns that wildlife authorities now face in managing the situation.

data.translatedTitle: Bangladesh chasing paltry total for first Test win in Australia

data.title: Boy charged over alleged McDonald’s stabbing
data.description: Witnesses reported an altercation between two boys at a restaurant north of Brisbane, one of whom suffered knife wounds to his abdomen.
data.translatedTitle: Boy charged over alleged McDonald’s stabbing
data.translatedDescription: Witnesses reported an altercation between two boys at a restaurant north of Brisbane, one of whom suffered knife wounds to his abdomen.

data.title: EN DIRECT, incendies et canicule : plus de 2 700 hectares ravagés en Belgique ; dans les Landes, le feu ne progresse plus mais n’est « pas en voie » d’être fixé
data.description: L’incendie qui s’est déclaré vendredi en milieu de journée dans les Hautes Fagnes, une grande zone boisée prisée des randonneurs et proche de l’Allemagne, est l’un des plus importants auquel a été confrontée la Belgique à ce jour.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, fires and heatwave: more than 2,700 hectares ravaged in Belgium; in the Landes, the fire is no longer progressing but is “not in the process” of being fixed
data.translatedDescription: The fire which broke out midday on Friday in the Hautes Fagnes, a large wooded area popular with hikers and close to Germany, is one of the largest that Belgium has faced to date.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : un blessé à Kiev après une attaque de missiles ; Moscou visée par 600 drones pendant la nuit
data.description: A Kryvy Rih, dans le centre de l’Ukraine, une personne a été tuée et six autres blessées. Par ailleurs, Moscou a été visée par 600 drones pendant la nuit, une attaque d’une rare ampleur qui a fait au moins trois blessés, selon le maire de la capitale russe.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, Ukraine war: One injured in kyiv after missile attack; Moscow targeted by 600 drones overnight
data.translatedDescription: In Kryvy Rih, central Ukraine, one person was killed and six others injured. Furthermore, Moscow was targeted by 600 drones during the night, an attack of rare magnitude which left at least three injured, according to the mayor of the Russian capital.

data.title: « Les luttes de faction à Téhéran pèsent sur les pourparlers avec les Etats-Unis »
data.description: Les gardiens de la révolution ne contrôlent pas seulement les opérations militaires, ils imposent aussi leurs exigences au président iranien et à ses négociateurs, analyse l’historien Jean-Pierre Filiu dans sa chronique.
data.translatedTitle: “Faction struggles in Tehran weigh on talks with US”
data.translatedDescription: The Revolutionary Guards not only control military operations, they also impose their demands on the Iranian president and his negotiators, analyzes historian Jean-Pierre Filiu in his column.

data.title: « Les questions que pose une famille qui veut s’installer, c’est : “Où est l’école et où peut-on se faire soigner ?” » : dans les Vosges, les maires essaient d’attirer les jeunes couples
data.description: Le département vosgien pourrait perdre un tiers de ses habitants d’ici à 2070. Un électrochoc pour les élus locaux, qui tentent de sauver leurs villages.
data.translatedTitle: “The questions a family asks when they want to settle down are: 'Where is the school and where can we get treatment?' »: in the Vosges, mayors are trying to attract young couples
data.translatedDescription: The Vosges department could lose a third of its inhabitants by 2070. A shock for local elected officials, who are trying to save their villages.

data.title: Championnats d’Europe de natation 2026 : Mary-Ambre Moluh, sacrée sur le 100 m dos, poursuit sa belle lancée vers les Jeux 2028
data.description: La Francilienne de 20 ans s’est offert une nouvelle médaille dans la compétition, samedi, quelques jours après s’être adjugé l’or sur le relais 4 × 100 m quatre nages mixte et l’argent sur le 50 m dos. Sa compatriote Pauline Mahieu est en bronze.
data.translatedTitle: 2026 European Swimming Championships: Mary-Ambre Moluh, crowned in the 100m backstroke, continues her strong momentum towards the 2028 Games
data.translatedDescription: The 20-year-old from Ile-de-France won a new medal in the competition on Saturday, a few days after winning gold in the 4 × 100m mixed medley relay and silver in the 50m backstroke. His compatriot Pauline Mahieu is in bronze.

data.title: L’Iran dénonce la détention de trois pilotes de chasse par le Qatar qui dément les avoir capturés
data.description: Téhéran affirme que ses trois soldats ont été récupérés par Doha après le crash de leurs avions, en mars, lors d’une attaque visant la base américaine d’Al-Udeid. Des « déclarations trompeuses », a répondu la diplomatie qatarie.
data.translatedTitle: Iran denounces the detention of three fighter pilots by Qatar which denies having captured them
data.translatedDescription: Tehran claims that its three soldiers were recovered by Doha after their planes crashed in March during an attack targeting the American base of Al-Udeid. “Misleading statements,” replied Qatari diplomacy.

data.title: Fortes pluies et coupures de courant : l’ouragan Lala menace Hawaï
data.description: Plus de 40 000 foyers sont déjà privés d’électricité et les autorités appellent à la vigilance face à des risques de crues soudaines. Lala pourrait déverser de 25 à 50 centimètres de pluie sur la Grande île, avec des cumuls dépassant 60 centimètres.
data.translatedTitle: Heavy rain and power outages: Hurricane Lala threatens Hawaii
data.translatedDescription: More than 40,000 homes are already without electricity and the authorities are calling for vigilance in the face of the risk of flash floods. Lala could dump 25 to 50 centimeters of rain on the Big Island, with accumulations exceeding 60 centimeters.

data.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Tondelier propose des « rencontres bilatérales » avec tous les partis de gauche
data.description: La cheffe des Ecologistes, qui maintient à ce stade sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle, s’est dite prête à « rediscuter avec tout le monde à gauche, sans exclusive » pour dégager « un chemin de victoire ».
data.translatedTitle: Presidential 2027: Marine Tondelier proposes “bilateral meetings” with all left-wing parties
data.translatedDescription: The leader of the Ecologists, who is maintaining her candidacy for the presidential election at this stage, said she was ready to “re-discuss with everyone on the left, without exception” to find “a path to victory”.

data.title: Meublé de tourisme : quand l’appartement n’a pas de fenêtre et que l’annonce ne le précise pas
data.description: Des voyageurs ont découvert à leur arrivée que la seule ouverture d’un logement situé dans le Morbihan est la porte d’entrée. Malgré les avis négatifs répétés, l’annonce est restée sur Booking.com.
data.translatedTitle: Furnished tourist accommodation: when the apartment does not have a window and the advert does not specify this
data.translatedDescription: Travelers discovered upon their arrival that the only opening to accommodation located in Morbihan is the front door. Despite repeated negative reviews, the ad remained on Booking.com.

data.title: Le nouveau président colombien demande à son allié Donald Trump de suspendre les droits de douane après le séisme
data.description: Abelardo de la Espriella a déclaré s’être entretenu avec son homologue américain, alors que les opérations de secours se poursuivent. A l’exception de certains produits, les droits de douane des Etats-Unis sur les produits colombiens sont passés de 10 % à 12,5 %, fin juillet.
data.translatedTitle: Colombia's new president asks his ally Donald Trump to suspend customs duties after the earthquake
data.translatedDescription: Abelardo de la Espriella said he spoke with his American counterpart as relief operations continue. With the exception of certain products, United States customs duties on Colombian products increased from 10% to 12.5% ​​at the end of July.

data.title: Le contrôle judiciaire de Patrick Bruel assoupli, le chanteur autorisé à quitter le territoire français
data.description: Un juge d’instruction a levé, le 21 juillet, à la demande des avocats du chanteur, son interdiction de quitter le territoire national, a fait savoir le parquet de Nanterre, qui a fait appel de cette décision.
data.translatedTitle: Judicial control of Patrick Bruel relaxed, the singer authorized to leave French territory
data.translatedDescription: An investigating judge lifted, on July 21, at the request of the singer's lawyers, his ban on leaving the national territory, reported the Nanterre prosecutor's office, which appealed this decision.

data.title: « Et, au fait, qui sait où est la pompe du paddle ? » : l’été à un accessoire près
data.description: « Les douleurs des vacances » (5/7). Tous les ans c’est la même histoire. Une roue de vélo dégonflée sans pompe, une tente sans sardines ou encore des raquettes sans balles. Et pourtant, ces objets restent dans les garages. Pourquoi est-ce si difficile de s’en séparer ?
data.translatedTitle: “And, by the way, who knows where the paddle pump is? »: summer with one accessory
data.translatedDescription: “Holiday Pains” (5/7). Every year it's the same story. A deflated bicycle wheel without a pump, a tent without pegs or even rackets without balls. And yet, these items remain in garages. Why is it so hard to part with it?

data.title: Isère : Laurent Nuñez et Aurore Bergé dénoncent les propos antisémites d’une commerçante, une enquête ouverte
data.description: Une enquête a été ouverte du chef de « provocation publique à la haine ou à la violence en raison de l’origine ou de la religion », selon le parquet de Grenoble. La commerçante, dont les propos ont été filmés, « a reconnu les propos tenus en expliquant le contexte dans lequel ils avaient été prononcés », précise-t-il.
data.translatedTitle: Isère: Laurent Nuñez and Aurore Bergé denounce the anti-Semitic comments of a shopkeeper, an open investigation
data.translatedDescription: An investigation was opened on the grounds of “public incitement to hatred or violence because of origin or religion”, according to the Grenoble public prosecutor’s office. The shopkeeper, whose remarks were filmed, “recognized the comments made by explaining the context in which they were said,” he specifies.

data.title: Les hommages se multiplient après la mort de Jason Arday, qui fut le plus jeune professeur noir de Cambridge, avant d’être accusé de plagiat
data.description: Plusieurs proches et collègues dénoncent aujourd’hui « un harcèlement » que le professeur de sociologie de l’éducation subissait depuis sa nomination il y a trois ans au sein de la prestigieuse université anglaise.
data.translatedTitle: Tributes multiply after the death of Jason Arday, who was the youngest black professor at Cambridge, before being accused of plagiarism
data.translatedDescription: Several relatives and colleagues are today denouncing “harassment” that the professor of sociology of education has suffered since his appointment three years ago at the prestigious English university.

data.title: Championnats d’Europe d’athlétisme : Jimmy Gressier décroche la médaille de bronze du 10 000 m
data.description: Le Français, champion du monde de la discipline, n’a rien pu faire face au Suédois Andreas Almgren, facile vainqueur, samedi. Mais s’adjuge tout de même, à 29 ans, le premier podium continental de sa carrière.
data.translatedTitle: European Athletics Championships: Jimmy Gressier wins bronze medal in the 10,000m
data.translatedDescription: The Frenchman, world champion in the discipline, was unable to do anything against the Swede Andreas Almgren, an easy winner on Saturday. But still won, at the age of 29, the first continental podium of his career.

data.title: Albanien: Scheitert das Bauprojekt der Trump-Familie an Massenprotesten und Korruptionsvorwürfen?
data.description: Jared Kushner will an der albanischen Küste ein Milliardenresort bauen. Doch im Umfeld des Projekts ermittelt die Staatsanwaltschaft wegen Geldwäsche und Kokainhandels, während der Protest im Land überkocht.
data.translatedTitle: Albania: Will the Trump family's construction project fail due to mass protests and allegations of corruption?
data.translatedDescription: Jared Kushner wants to build a billion dollar resort on the Albanian coast. But the public prosecutor's office is investigating money laundering and cocaine trafficking in the area surrounding the project, while the protests in the country are boiling over.

data.title: Ukraine: Drohnenangriffe aus Russland – der Highway der verbrannten Tankstellen
data.description: Tanken kann in der Ukraine lebensgefährlich sein: Entlang einer wichtigen Fernstraße stürzen sich russische Drohnen auf Tankstellen, mehr als 200 sind schon in Flammen aufgegangen. Die Ukrainer reagieren mit Trotz.
data.translatedTitle: Ukraine: Drone attacks from Russia – the highway of burned gas stations
data.translatedDescription: Refueling in Ukraine can be life-threatening: Russian drones are descending on gas stations along an important highway, and more than 200 have already burst into flames. The Ukrainians react with defiance.

data.title: Manuela Schwesig: Senderchef deutet in Chatnachricht Einmischung bei TV-Duell an
data.description: Hat Mecklenburg-Vorpommerns Ministerpräsidentin zwei Herausforderer aus einer TV-Debatte zur Landtagswahl gedrängt? Die Chatnachricht eines Verantwortlichen, die dem SPIEGEL vorliegt, nährt diesen Verdacht.
data.translatedTitle: Manuela Schwesig: Channel boss indicates interference in TV duel in chat message
data.translatedDescription: Did Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania's Prime Minister force two challengers out of a TV debate in the state election? The chat message from one of those responsible, which SPIEGEL has received, fuels this suspicion.

data.title: Friedrich Merz: Was der Vergleich mit Angela Merkel über die CDU verrät
data.description: Kanzlerin Merkel hat 16 lange Jahre regiert, ihr Nachfolger Merz ist schon nach kurzer Zeit angeschlagen. Dafür gibt es Gründe, die in den Personen, aber auch in der Gesellschaft liegen.
data.translatedTitle: Friedrich Merz: What the comparison with Angela Merkel reveals about the CDU
data.translatedDescription: Chancellor Merkel ruled for 16 long years, and her successor Merz fell ill after just a short time. There are reasons for this that lie in people, but also in society.

data.title: Ceuta: Marokko meldet mehr als hundert Festnahmen nach Grenzübertrittsversuche
data.description: In sozialen Netzwerken gibt es erneute Aufrufe zum Grenzübertritt nach Ceuta. Marokkanische Sicherheitskräfte nahmen mehr als hundert Menschen fest und setzten offenbar Tränengas ein.
data.translatedTitle: Ceuta: Morocco reports more than a hundred arrests after border crossing attempts
data.translatedDescription: There are renewed calls on social networks to cross the border to Ceuta. Moroccan security forces arrested more than a hundred people and apparently used tear gas.

data.title: Jason Arday: Andy Burnham bezeichnet Tod von Cambridge-Professor als »Tragödie«
data.description: Nach dem Tod des früheren Professors der Universität Cambridge, Jason Arday, herrscht in Großbritannien Bestürzung. Nun sei nicht die Zeit für »voreilige Urteile«, so Premier Andy Burnham. »Es ist ein Moment der Reflexion.«
data.translatedTitle: Jason Arday: Andy Burnham calls Cambridge professor's death a "tragedy"
data.translatedDescription: There is consternation in Great Britain following the death of former Cambridge University professor Jason Arday. Now is not the time for “hasty judgments,” said Prime Minister Andy Burnham. "It's a moment of reflection."

data.title: Hurrikan »Lala« erreicht Hawaii
data.description: Der tropische Sturm »Lala« hat sich zum Hurrikan verstärkt und zieht dicht an Hawaiis Hauptinsel vorbei. Tausende sind bereits ohne Strom, Straßen überflutet. Auch die Inseln Maui und Oahu müssen sich auf Sturm und Starkregen einstellen.
data.translatedTitle: Hurricane Lala hits Hawaii
data.translatedDescription: The tropical storm "Lala" has strengthened into a hurricane and is passing close to Hawaii's main island. Thousands are already without power and streets are flooded. The islands of Maui and Oahu also have to prepare for storms and heavy rain.

data.title: Waldbrände in Belgien näher an Grenze gerückt – Feuerwehr wässert Felder bei Monschau
data.description: Die in Belgien lodernden Brände sind noch rund drei Kilometer von der deutschen Grenze entfernt. Rund 5000 Einwohner der nordrhein-westfälischen Stadt Monschau bereiten sich auf eine Evakuierung vor – eine akute Gefahr besteht jedoch vorerst nicht.
data.translatedTitle: Forest fires in Belgium have moved closer to the border – firefighters are watering fields near Monschau
data.translatedDescription: The fires blazing in Belgium are still around three kilometers from the German border. Around 5,000 residents of the North Rhine-Westphalian town of Monschau are preparing to evacuate - but there is currently no acute danger.

data.title: Waldbrand in der Eifel: Bewohner dürfen nach Hürtgenwald zurückkehren
data.description: Die Lage im Waldbrandgebiet in Nordrhein-Westfalen konnte stabilisiert werden. Jetzt erhielten die zuvor evakuierten Menschen eine erleichternde Nachricht: Sie können wieder nach Hause.
data.translatedTitle: Forest fire in the Eifel: Residents are allowed to return to Hürtgenwald
data.translatedDescription: The situation in the forest fire area in North Rhine-Westphalia has been stabilized. Now the people who had previously been evacuated received a relieving message: they can go home again.

data.title: »The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild«: Platz eins im SPIEGEL-Games-Kanon
data.description: Videospiele bieten, anders als Filme und Bücher, das Gefühl von Freiheit. Und in keinem anderen fühlen sich die Möglichkeiten so endlos an wie in »The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild«. Platz eins im SPIEGEL-Games-Kanon.
data.translatedTitle: »The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild«: Platz eins im SPIEGEL-Games-Kanon
data.translatedDescription: Unlike films and books, video games offer a feeling of freedom. And in no other place do the possibilities feel as endless as in “The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild”. First place in the SPIEGEL Games canon.

data.title: Kolumbiens Armee entdeckt Drogenlabor mit 1,8 Tonnen Kokain
data.description: Im Kampf gegen den Drogenhandel kann die neue kolumbianische Regierung einen ersten Erfolg verbuchen. Staatschef Abelardo de la Espriella ordnet die zerstörte illegale Produktionsstätte einer linken Rebellengruppe zu.
data.translatedTitle: Colombia's army discovers drug lab with 1.8 tons of cocaine
data.translatedDescription: The new Colombian government has achieved initial success in the fight against drug trafficking. Head of State Abelardo de la Espriella attributes the destroyed illegal production facility to a left-wing rebel group.

data.title: Tausende Fans nehmen Abschied von Rocksängerin Bonnie Tyler
data.description: Die raue Stimme war ihr Markenzeichen, ihre Powerballaden machten Bonnie Tyler zum Weltstar. Jetzt hat ihre walisische Heimatstadt Mumbles der Rocksängerin einen bewegenden Abschied bereitet.
data.translatedTitle: Thousands of fans say goodbye to rock singer Bonnie Tyler
data.translatedDescription: The rough voice was her trademark, her power ballads made Bonnie Tyler a global star. Now her Welsh hometown of Mumbles has given the rock singer a moving farewell.

data.title: Flughafen München: Vietnam Airlines Maschine hebt spät ab und dreht um
data.description: Beim Start wirbelte das Flugzeug von Vietnam Airlines viel Staub auf, bei der Landung nach der außerplanmäßigen Rückkehr zum Münchner Flughafen lösten sich Teile der Reifen ab. Wie es zu dem Vorfall kam, war zunächst unklar.
data.translatedTitle: Munich Airport: Vietnam Airlines plane takes off late and turns around
data.translatedDescription: The Vietnam Airlines plane kicked up a lot of dust when it took off, and parts of the tires came off when it landed after the unscheduled return to Munich Airport. It was initially unclear how the incident occurred.

data.title: Australien: New South Wales startet Waffenrückkauf nach Bondi-Beach-Attentat
data.description: Nach dem antisemitischen Angriff bei einer Chanukka-Feier sollen Besitzer neu verbotener Pistolen und Gewehre ihre Waffen gegen Entschädigung abgeben. Andere australische Bundesstaaten könnten folgen.
data.translatedTitle: Australia: New South Wales starts arms sales after Bondi Beach attack
data.translatedDescription: After the anti-Semitic attack at a Hanukkah celebration, owners of newly banned pistols and rifles should hand in their weapons for compensation. Other Australian states could follow suit.

data.title: Thronfolge in Liechtenstein: Fürstenhaus schafft männliches Erstgeburtsrecht ab
data.description: Das Fürstenhaus schafft das männliche Erstgeburtsrecht ab. Künftig soll das älteste Kind den Thron erben – unabhängig davon, ob es ein Sohn oder eine Tochter ist.
data.translatedTitle: Succession to the throne in Liechtenstein: Princely House abolishes male birthright
data.translatedDescription: The royal family abolishes male birthright. In the future, the eldest child will inherit the throne - regardless of whether it is a son or a daughter.

data.title: Sizilien: Flugbetrieb in Catania nach Ätna-Ausbruch wieder aufgenommen
data.description: Vor mehr als einer Woche war der Ätna auf Sizilien ausgebrochen, Tausende Urlauber konnten die Insel wegen der Schließung des Flughafens in Catania nicht verlassen. Nun wurde der Flugbetrieb wieder aufgenommen.
data.translatedTitle: Sicily: Flight operations resumed in Catania after Etna eruption
data.translatedDescription: More than a week ago, Mount Etna in Sicily erupted and thousands of holidaymakers were unable to leave the island because the airport in Catania was closed. Flight operations have now resumed.

data.title: Leichtathletik-EM in Birmingham: Julian Weber wirft Speer im letzten Versuch zu Gold
data.description: Speerwerfer Julian Weber hat sich trotz Schulterproblemen in einem dramatischen Finale EM-Gold gesichert. Er übertraf dabei die 90-Meter-Marke. Nick Thumm gewann Silber – genau wie die deutsche Sprinstaffel der Männer.
data.translatedTitle: European Athletics Championships in Birmingham: Julian Weber throws javelin in the last attempt for gold
data.translatedDescription: Javelin thrower Julian Weber secured European Championship gold in a dramatic final despite shoulder problems. He exceeded the 90 meter mark. Nick Thumm won silver – as did the German men’s sprint relay.

data.title: Schwimm-EM in Paris: Liebmann holt Gold mit Weltrekord über 1500 Meter
data.description: Nachwuchsstar Johannes Liebmann hat im Becken von Paris Schwimmgeschichte geschrieben: Der 19-Jährige siegte in Weltrekordzeit. Bronze ging an seinen Teamkollegen Oliver Klemet.
data.translatedTitle: European Swimming Championships in Paris: Liebmann wins gold with a world record in the 1500 meters
data.translatedDescription: Young star Johannes Liebmann made swimming history in the Paris pool: The 19-year-old won in a world record time. Bronze went to his teammate Oliver Klemet.

data.title: Supercup: Wolfsburgerin Johannes unterlaufen Patzer – Bayern siegt erneut
data.description: Die Fußballerinnen des FC Bayern München enteilen dem Erzrivalen Wolfsburg. Dabei schienen die Teams lange gleich stark, ehe Torhüterin Stina Johannes zwei unglückliche Momente erlebte.
data.translatedTitle: Supercup: Wolfsburg's Johannes makes a mistake - Bayern wins again
data.translatedDescription: The footballers of FC Bayern Munich are away from their arch-rivals Wolfsburg. The teams seemed equally strong for a long time before goalkeeper Stina Johannes experienced two unfortunate moments.

data.title: Jürgen Klopp: Der Bundestrainer relativiert seine »Medienschelte«
data.description: Mit Aussagen zur Rolle der Medien hatte Jürgen Klopp zuletzt irritiert. Nun stellte der Bundestrainer klar, dass es ihm lediglich um Attacken des Boulevards gegangen sei – und räumte mit einem Gerücht um Saïd El Mala auf.
data.translatedTitle: Jürgen Klopp: The national coach puts his “media scolding” into perspective
data.translatedDescription: Jürgen Klopp recently irritated people with statements about the role of the media. Now the national coach made it clear that he was only interested in attacks from the tabloids - and cleared up a rumor about Saïd El Mala.

data.title: Außerirdisches Leben: Astrophysiker Michael Garrett über Risiken eines Alien-Kontakts
data.description: Der Astrophysiker Michael Garrett hat eine Anleitung verfasst, wie seine Kollegen vorgehen sollen, wenn sie außerirdisches Leben finden. Hier spricht er über Gefahren für die Menschheit und darüber, woher die Ufos kommen.
data.translatedTitle: Extraterrestrial life: Astrophysicist Michael Garrett on the risks of alien contact
data.translatedDescription: Astrophysicist Michael Garrett has written a guide on what his colleagues should do if they find extraterrestrial life. Here he talks about dangers to humanity and where UFOs come from.

data.title: VW-Bus: Der Traum vom gebrauchten Bulli – und warum er so häufig platzt
data.description: Wer sich einen gebrauchten VW-Bus zulegt, wird oft enttäuscht: Viele Modelle haben starken Verschleiß und weisen zahlreiche Mängel auf. Manchem Bulli-Besitzer wird zu spät klar, worauf man hätte achten müssen.
data.translatedTitle: VW bus: The dream of a used van - and why it bursts so often
data.translatedDescription: Anyone who buys a used VW bus is often disappointed: many models are heavily worn and have numerous defects. Some Bulli owners realize too late what they should have paid attention to.

data.title: Geldanlage: Was man als ETF-Anfänger wissen muss
data.description: Globale Krisen und düstere Stimmung machen die Entscheidung für Geldanlagen nicht gerade einfach. Finanzexperte Hartmut Walz gibt Tipps und weiß, welche Strategien sich bewährt haben.
data.translatedTitle: Investing: What you need to know as an ETF beginner
data.translatedDescription: Global crises and a gloomy mood make the decision to invest not exactly easy. Financial expert Hartmut Walz gives tips and knows which strategies have proven successful.

data.title: Eberhofer-Krimi »Steckerlfischfiasko« im Kino: Rita Falk über Grenzen des Humors
data.description: Die Schriftstellerin Rita Falk hatte sich zuletzt lautstark geärgert über eine Kinoverfilmung ihrer erfolgreichen Eberhofer-Krimis. Wie findet sie den neuen Eberhofer-Film »Steckerlfischfiasko«?
data.translatedTitle: Eberhofer crime thriller “Steckerlfischfiasco” in the cinema: Rita Falk on the limits of humor

data.translatedTitle: 'Yeah, sleep'
data.translatedDescription: It appeared in my feed: "Hey Gil, what do you like to do most in life?" "Sleep." The interviewer is startled. "Sleeping?! Really?! More than singing?!". "Because it's good, it's a feeling of total surrender to existence. It's existence without the excessive mediation of the self. Without the excessive demands of the ego. data.title: Skrällsilver till Samuel Pihlström på 1500 meter
data.description: BIRMINGHAM. En dryg kvart efter Andreas Almgrens guld på 10 000 meter kom nästa svenska EM-medalj. Samuel Pihlström svarade för en stor skräll på 1 500 meter. I en mäktig slutspurt gick han om löpare efter löpare – och tog silver. – Det är svårt att sätta ord på det här, säger han.
data.translatedTitle: Silver medal for Samuel Pihlström in 1500 meters
data.translatedDescription: BIRMINGHAM. Just over a quarter of an hour after Andreas Almgren's gold in the 10,000 meters came the next Swedish European Championship medal. Samuel Pihlström answered for a big bang in the 1,500 meters. In a powerful final sprint, he overtook runner after runner - and took silver. - It is difficult to put this into words, he says.

data.title: Almgrens slakt på EM – vann guld överlägset: ”Kan inte bli bättre”
data.description: BIRMINGHAM. VM-brons i fjol – EM-guld i år. Andreas Almgren fortsätter att bryta ny mark i långdistanslöpning. I Birmingham var 31-åringen fullständigt överlägsen på 10 000 meter – och skrev svensk friidrottshistoria. – Det kan inte bli bättre, säger Andreas Almgren.
data.translatedTitle: Almgren's slaughter at the European Championships - won gold by far: "Can't get better"
data.translatedDescription: BIRMINGHAM. WC bronze last year – EC gold this year. Andreas Almgren continues to break new ground in long-distance running. In Birmingham, the 31-year-old was completely superior in the 10,000 meters - and wrote Swedish athletics history. - It can't get any better, says Andreas Almgren.

Under Alf Svensson stod Kristdemokraterna för solidaritet och kristen etik, men under Ebba Busch elva år vid rodret har partiet förvandlats till en nationalistisk mur där svenskhet går före tro. Now the Christian heritage is used to exclude rather than unite. The result? The religious voters have turned their backs on the party, write two religious scholars.
